text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President Hosni Mubarak receives telephone calls from King Hussein, Palestinian President Arafat and U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher...and a Palestinian-Israeli summit meeting is expected within hours.
- Tunis beats the Egyptian football league 1-0 in the World Cup qualifier.

- Government to sell 16 profitable spinning, weaving and external trade companies in addition to food manufacturers and construction firms. Firms have a total value of 2.7 billion pounds and the state will start by selling 10 percent.
- Insurance firms allowed to invest their money in the Egyptian securities market.
- State decides to implement new petroleum projects to provide energy for construction work in the new delta.
- Hebron accord to be initialed today. Arafat calls Mubarak to brief him on the latest developments.

- Egyptian ambassador to Washington responds to Israeli accusations and tells Washington Post that Egypt supports peace and having a peace deal between the Palestinians and Israelis is in Egypt's interest.
- State cuts interest on loans for land reclamation to around six percent to encourage investment.
- Ancient Roman city discovered near Nile Delta province of Damietta.
- Egyptian bus driver dies at wheel in Cairo traffic.
